tasks.title: Mixed exam — Reading a clearance plot
tasks.context: On the axes below, a **solid brown parabola** and a **dashed green line** model clearance for MetroLink. Coefficients are not printed on the diagram. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The solid curve and the dashed line meet in exactly two points.
The turning point of the solid curve lies below the dashed line.
At the integer mark $x=0$ the dashed line sits above the solid curve.
The solid curve opens upwards.
At the integer mark $x=3$ the dashed line is higher than the solid curve.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Two graphs meet where their heights agree, so the crossings on the sketch are the real zeros of the difference.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 1$$

$$f(x)=x - 3$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 3 x + 4$$

A quadratic difference has at most two real zeros; the discriminant decides how many actually occur.

$$\Delta=25$$

The discriminant is positive and the plot shows two crossings, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The turning point sits on the axis of the parabola. Recover that abscissa from the reconstructed coefficients, then compare heights.

$$x=-\frac{4}{2\cdot \left(-1\right)}=2$$

$$g\left(2\right)=5$$

$$f\left(2\right)=-1$$

The turning height sits above the dashed line, not below it, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Compare the two heights on the vertical axis, which is the integer mark $x=0$.

$$g(0)=1$$

$$f(0)=-3$$

The signed gap dashed-minus-solid is therefore negative, so the solid curve is the higher of the two.

$$f(0)-g(0)=-4$$

At $x=0$ the solid curve sits above the dashed line, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

A parabola opens upwards only when its leading coefficient is positive. The reconstructed solid curve is

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 1$$

$$a=-1$$

A negative leading coefficient turns the arms down, which is also why the marked turning point is a peak rather than a trough.

The solid curve opens downwards, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Read both heights at the tick $x=3$ on the horizontal axis, then confirm by substituting into the reconstructed models.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 1$$

$$g(3)=4$$

$$f(x)=x - 3$$

$$f(3)=0$$

The solid height $4$ sits above the dashed height $0$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The figure is the only source. Reconstructing the two models gives $f(x)=x - 3$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 1$. The vertex is $\left(2,5\right)$ and the graphs meet 2 times.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — SkyLift sequence
tasks.context: SkyLift logs discrete readings $s_n$ for $n=0,1,2,\ldots$ in the table. No closed form is supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Diagnosing the table by successive differences, the sequence is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$.
The first differences are constant, so the sequence is linear.
Extrapolating one step beyond the table gives $s_{7}=15$.
After the quadratic is rebuilt, its axis is $n=4$.
A linear model fitted to the first two samples predicts $s_{4}$ correctly.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A quadratic sequence $s_n=an^{2}+bn+c$ has constant second differences equal to $2a$. Build the first differences from the raw row, then the second differences from those.

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(-5,-3,-1,1,3,5)$$

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

$$2a=2\Rightarrow a=1$$

The constant $2$ forces leading coefficient $1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

A linear sequence is the unique case in which first differences do not change. The first differences of this row are

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(-5,-3,-1,1,3,5)$$

Those steps themselves grow by $2$ each time, which is the signature of a quadratic, not a line.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

Growing first differences rule out a linear model, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Once $a$ is known from the second differences, the opening first difference $a+b$ and the $n=0$ entry recover $b$ and $c$.

$$a=1,\quad a+b=-5\Rightarrow b=-6$$

$$c=s_0=8$$

The same rule evaluated at $n=7$ is the extrapolated term.

$$s_7=1\cdot 7^{2}+(-6)\cdot 7+8=15$$

The next term is $15$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The axis of $an^{2}+bn+c$ is $n=-b/(2a)$. With $a=1$ and $b=-6$

$$n=-\frac{-6}{2\cdot 1}=3$$

The axis is $n=3$, not $n=4$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The unique line through the first two samples has slope $s_1-s_0$ and intercept $s_0$.

$$s_n=8+(-5)n$$

$$s_4^{\text{lin}}=-12$$

The table's quadratic rule gives a different value at $n=4$.

$$s_4=0$$

The linear extrapolation misses $s_4$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Only the raw row is given. Constant second differences $\Delta^{(2)}=2$ rebuild $s_n=1n^{2}-6n+8$, with axis $n=3$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — HarborCrane operations
tasks.context: HarborCrane logs fare (euros) and bridge clearance (metres) against load $x$ (tonnes) in the table. No closed form is on file. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The clearance row is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$.
The fare row is linear with slope $4$.
Among the integer loads in the table, clearance is lowest at $x=3$.
If the same linear fare and quadratic clearance continue off the table, they meet twice.
At the axis of clearance, clearance exceeds fare.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Second differences of a quadratic row equal $2a$. From the clearance values

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(-5,-3,-1,1)$$

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

$$a=\frac{2}{2}=1$$

Clearance is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

A linear row has constant first differences, and that constant is the slope.

$$\Delta^{(1)}_{\text{fare}}=(3,3,3,3)$$

$$m=3$$

The fare slope is $3$, not $4$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

The axis of the rebuilt clearance parabola is $x=-b/(2a)$. With $a=1$ and $a+b$ equal to the opening clearance step

$$b=-6,\quad x=3$$

That axis is an integer column of the table, and the vertex of an upward parabola is its lowest point.

$$g\left(3\right)=-4$$

The sampled minimum sits at $x=3$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Meetings are the real zeros of the rebuilt difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 9 x + 3$$

$$\Delta=69$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Evaluate both rebuilt models on the clearance axis $x=3$.

$$f(3)=11$$

$$g(3)=-4$$

Fare $11$ exceeds clearance $-4$ on that axis, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The table is the only numeric source. Fitting gives $f(x)=3 x + 2$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$; axis $x=3$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 1
tasks.context: A non-constant line $f$ and a quadratic $g$ with nonzero leading coefficient meet through the difference $d(x)=g(x)-f(x)$. No numeric data are supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Unless the slope of $f$ vanishes, the axis of $d$ differs from the axis of $g$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $d$ equals the leading coefficient of $g$.
If the graphs of $f$ and $g$ are tangent, the vertex of $d$ lies on the horizontal axis.
Nesting always adds the degrees: the highest power of $g(f(x))$ equals the sum of the degrees of $g$ and $f$.
The function $d$ has a smallest value exactly when $a>0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Subtracting a slanted line leaves the square term of $g$ untouched but shifts the linear coefficient.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-k)$$

An axis depends only on the first two coefficients, so the two axes split by a term proportional to the slope.

$$x_{d}-x_{g}=\frac{m}{2a}$$

A nonzero slope moves the axis of the difference, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

A line has no square term to contribute, so the subtraction cannot change the leading coefficient of $g$.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-k)$$

The square-term coefficient of $d$ is still $a$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Tangency means $g=f$ has a repeated root, so $d$ has a double zero. A double zero of a parabola sits at its vertex, and the value there is zero.

$$d(x)=a\left(x-x_{0}\right)^{2}$$

$$d\left(x_{0}\right)=0$$

A vertex of height zero lies on the horizontal axis, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Degrees add under multiplication and multiply under substitution. Putting a line inside a parabola squares a linear expression and stops at the second power.

$$g(f(x))=a(mx+k)^{2}+b(mx+k)+c$$

$$a(mx+k)^{2}=am^{2}x^{2}+\cdots$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$, the product of the two degrees, not their sum, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

The difference inherits the leading coefficient of $g$, so it opens the same way $g$ does. An upward parabola is bounded below by its vertex; a downward one is not bounded below at all.

$$a>0\Rightarrow d(x)\geq d\left(x_{d}\right)$$

A smallest value exists precisely when the leading coefficient is positive, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Pure line–parabola reasoning: $d=g-f$ keeps the square term of $g$, shifts the axis when the slope is nonzero, and has a minimum exactly when it opens upwards.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — ArenaLights parameter sweep
tasks.context: ArenaLights tests clearance families $g_t(x)=x^{2}-2tx+t$ against $f(x)=2 x - 1$. Take $t=2$ for the run under review, and study how $\Delta(t)$ changes with $t$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: With $t=2$, the graphs meet in two distinct points (they are not tangent).
Tangency occurs at $t=0$.
For $t=3$ the graphs meet twice.
For every real $t$ the difference $g_t-f$ is quadratic in $x$, so there are at most two intersection points.
There exists a real $t$ making $\Delta(t)=0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Tangency is a vanishing discriminant of $g_t-f$. Expanding that discriminant as a function of $t$ gives

$$\Delta(t)=4 t \left(t + 1\right)$$

$$\Delta\left(2\right)=24$$

A positive value means two distinct meetings, not a tangency, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The discriminant factors as $4t(t+1)$, so it vanishes at $t=0$ and at $t=-1$.

$$\Delta(t)=4 t \left(t + 1\right)$$

$$\Delta(0)=0$$

The value $t=0$ is a tangency parameter, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Substitute $t=3$ into the same discriminant.

$$\Delta(3)=48$$

A positive discriminant at $t=3$ gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The parameter $t$ sits in the linear and constant terms, never in a cube.

$$g_t(x)-f(x)=x^{2}-(2t+2)x+(t+1)$$

A quadratic in $x$ has at most two real zeros for any $t$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The factored discriminant $4t(t+1)$ has two real roots.

$$t=0\quad\text{and}\quad t=-1$$

Tangency occurs for at least one real parameter, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Family $g_t$ versus $f(x)=2 x - 1$. Discriminant $\Delta(t)=4 t \left(t + 1\right)$; at $t=2$ there are two meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Aqueduct reconstruction
tasks.context: A line through $(1,2)$ with slope $3$ meets a parabola whose vertex is $(2,-3)$ and whose leading coefficient is $1$. Rebuild both formulas for Aqueduct, then judge each claim. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The rebuilt line is $f(x)=3 x - 1$.
The rebuilt parabola is $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+3$.
The rebuilt curves meet in exactly one point.
The axis of the rebuilt parabola is $x=3$.
The vertex height is $0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Point-slope form uses the given slope and the given point.

$$f(x)=3\left(x-1\right)+2$$

$$f(x)=3 x - 1$$

The reconstructed line matches the data, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Vertex form with the given turning point and leading coefficient $1$ is

$$g(x)=\left(x-2\right)^{2}+-3$$

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 1$$

The constant term is $1$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Meetings are the real zeros of $g-f$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 7 x + 2$$

$$\Delta=41$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, not one, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The axis is the abscissa of the given vertex, equivalently $-b/(2a)$ after expansion.

$$x=2$$

The axis is $x=2$, not $x=3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The vertex height is the value of $g$ on its axis, which was part of the given turning point.

$$g\left(2\right)=-3$$

The vertex height is $-3$, not $0$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Rebuilt $f(x)=3 x - 1$, $g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 1$; vertex $\left(2,-3\right)$; 2 meetings; rewrite $A=\frac{1}{9}$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Orchard compositions
tasks.context: Composition drills for Orchard: $f(x)=2 x - 1$, $g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 1$. Expand before trusting degree shortcuts. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The highest power of $f(g(x))$ equals the highest power of $g(f(x))$.
The highest power of $g(f(x))$ is $x^{3}$.
The axis of $g(f)$ equals the axis of $g$.
$f(g(1))$ equals $g(f(1))$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Substitute the line into the parabola and expand, term by term.

$$g(f(x))=g\left(2 x - 1\right)$$

$$(2 x - 1)^{2}-4(2 x - 1)+1$$

$$g(f(x))=4 x^{2} - 12 x + 6$$

The expanded composition matches the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Highest powers multiply under substitution. Both orders use degrees $1$ and $2$, so both close at $x^{2}$. Expanding the other order confirms it.

$$f(g(x))=2 x^{2} - 8 x + 1$$

$$g(f(x))=4 x^{2} - 12 x + 6$$

Both compositions are quadratic, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Squaring a linear expression reaches $x^{2}$ and stops; the remaining terms of $g$ are linear or constant in $f$.

$$g(f(x))=4 x^{2} - 12 x + 6$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Each parabola has its own axis, computed from its own first two coefficients.

$$x_{g(f)}=\frac{3}{2}$$

$$x_g=2$$

The axes are $\frac{3}{2}$ and $2$, which are not equal, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The two orders of substitution are different functions. Evaluate each at $1$.

$$g(1)=-2$$

$$f(g(1))=-5$$

$$g(f(1))=-2$$

The two values are $-5$ and $-2$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Compositions $g(f(x))=4 x^{2} - 12 x + 6$ and $f(g(x))=2 x^{2} - 8 x + 1$. Highest powers multiply; axes of $g(f)$ and $g$ need not agree.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — RaceTrack factored parabola
tasks.context: At RaceTrack the parabola is given in factored form $g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)$ and the line is $f(x)=2 x - 2$. Use Vieta, the axis, and the discriminant of $g-f$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis is the midpoint of the roots, so $x=3$.
The product of the roots is $5$.
The vertex height is $-4$.
The line and the parabola meet in exactly one point.
The factored parabola opens downwards.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A factored monic parabola $g(x)=(x-r_1)(x-r_2)$ has axis at the midpoint of the roots, which is also $-b/(2a)$ after expansion.

$$x=\frac{1+5}{2}=3$$

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

The axis is $x=3$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Vieta reads the product from the constant term of a monic quadratic, and also as the product of the displayed roots.

$$P=1\cdot 5=5$$

$$P=\frac{c}{a}=5$$

The product is $5$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The axis is already the midpoint $x=3$. Evaluate the factored form there, then cross-check against the expansion.

$$g\left(3\right)=(3-1)(3-5)=-4$$

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

$$g(3)=9-18+5=-4$$

The vertex height is $-4$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The difference $g-f$ is still quadratic. Its discriminant decides the meeting count.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 7$$

$$\Delta=36$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The leading coefficient of $(x-1)(x-5)$ is $+1$.

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

$$a=1$$

A positive leading coefficient opens the parabola upwards, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Factored $g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)$; roots $1,5$; axis $x=3$; $P=5$; 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — ZipLine hybrid check
tasks.context: ZipLine supplies a figure (solid brown parabola, dashed green line) and a raw table of the solid curve's integer samples. No closed form is printed. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the figure, the solid curve opens downwards.
From the figure, the graphs meet in exactly two points.
From the table, successive differences show that the sampled sequence is quadratic with leading coefficient $-1$.
From the table, extrapolating one step gives $s_{5}=0$.
After fitting the table, the axis is $x=4$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Opening is visible on the sketch as a peak rather than a trough, and it matches the reconstructed leading coefficient.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 6 x - 5$$

$$a=-1$$

A negative leading coefficient opens the solid curve downwards, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Count the crossings of the solid stroke against the dashed stroke, then confirm with the discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 5 x - 3$$

$$\Delta=13$$

Two visible crossings match a positive discriminant, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Build differences from the raw $s_n$ row (the figure is not needed for this letter).

$$\Delta^{(2)}=-2$$

$$a=\frac{-2}{2}=-1$$

The table rebuilds leading coefficient $-1$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The same rebuilt rule $s_n=-n^{2}+6n-5$ is evaluated at the first missing index.

$$s_5=-5^{2}+6\cdot 5-5=0$$

The next term is $0$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

With $a=-1$ and $a+b$ equal to the opening first difference, $b=6$ and the axis is

$$x=-\frac{6}{2\cdot (-1)}=3$$

The axis is $x=3$, not $x=4$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Figure plus table, no printed formulae. Reconstructing gives $f(x)=x - 2$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 6 x - 5$; axis $x=3$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Velodrome dense briefing
tasks.context: At Velodrome a line of slope $4$ through $(0,-3)$ is used together with a monic parabola whose roots are $1$ and $3$. Recover both models from that sentence, then test each claim. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis of the parabola is $x=2$.
The vertex height is $-1$.
The line and the parabola meet twice.
The product of the roots is $3$.
The $y$-intercept of the line is $-3$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A monic parabola with roots $1$ and $3$ expands to $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+3$. The axis is both the midpoint of the roots and $-b/(2a)$.

$$g(x)=(x-1)(x-3)=x^{2}-4x+3$$

$$x=\frac{1+3}{2}=2$$

$$x=-\frac{-4}{2\cdot 1}=2$$

Both routes give axis $x=2$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Evaluate the monic factored form on the axis already recovered as $x=2$.

$$g(x)=(x-1)(x-3)$$

$$g(2)=(2-1)(2-3)=-1$$

The same height comes from substituting into the expansion $x^{2}-4x+3$.

$$g(2)=4-8+3=-1$$

The vertex height is $-1$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The line through $(0,-3)$ with slope $4$ is $f(x)=4x-3$. Subtract from $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+3$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 6$$

$$\Delta=40$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The two given roots multiply to $3$, and Vieta on the expansion agrees.

$$P=1\cdot 3=3$$

The product is $3$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

A line of slope $4$ through $(0,-3)$ already displays its intercept.

$$f(x)=4 x - 3$$

$$f(0)=-3$$

The intercept is $-3$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: The dense sentence rebuilds $f(x)=4 x - 3$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 3$; axis $x=2$, vertex height $-1$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Vertex against the service line
tasks.context: On the axes below, a **solid brown parabola** and a **dashed green line** model clearance for CoastGuard. Coefficients are not printed on the diagram. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The graphs meet in more than two points.
The turning point of the solid curve lies below the dashed line.
The solid curve opens downwards.
At $x=0$ the solid curve sits above the dashed line.
At the integer mark $x=4$ the solid curve is higher than the dashed line.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

A line and a parabola differ by a quadratic, so they cannot meet three times.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 13$$

$$\Delta=12$$

A positive discriminant supplies two distinct real meetings and no more.

$$2$$

The count is two, never more than two, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

Locate the axis of the solid curve, evaluate both models there, and compare.

$$x=3$$

$$g\left(3\right)=-4$$

$$f\left(3\right)=-2$$

The turning height $-4$ sits below the dashed height $-2$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Opening is the sign of the leading coefficient alone.

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

$$a=1$$

A positive leading coefficient sends the arms up, so the marked turning point is a trough.

The solid curve opens upwards, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

The vertical axis is the integer mark $x=0$; read the two intercepts and subtract.

$$g(0)=5$$

$$f(0)=-8$$

$$g(0)-f(0)=13$$

The solid intercept $5$ sits well above the dashed intercept $-8$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Compare heights at the tick $x=4$.

$$g(4)=-3$$

$$f(4)=0$$

The dashed height $0$ sits above the solid height $-3$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The figure is the only source. Reconstructing the two models gives $f(x)=2 x - 8$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$. The vertex is $\left(3,-4\right)$ and the graphs meet 2 times.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — IceRink readings
tasks.context: IceRink logs discrete readings $s_n$ for $n=0,1,2,\ldots$ in the table. No closed form is supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Diagnosing the table by successive differences, the leading coefficient is $1$.
The rebuilt discrete quadratic has its axis at $n=3$.
Extrapolating one step beyond the table gives $s_{6}=13$.
The first differences grow by $2$ at each step, confirming that the sequence has degree $2$.
A linear model through the first two samples predicts $s_{4}$ correctly.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Compute successive differences from the raw row.

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(-3,-1,1,3,5)$$

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

$$a=\frac{\Delta^{(2)}}{2}=1$$

The leading coefficient is $1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

From $2a=2$ and $a+b=s_1-s_0$ the linear coefficient follows, and then the axis.

$$a=1,\quad b=-4$$

$$n=-\frac{-4}{2\cdot 1}=2$$

The axis is $n=2$, not $n=3$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

The rebuilt rule is $s_n=n^{2}-4n+1$. One further index is then a substitution.

$$s_6=6^{2}-4\cdot 6+1=13$$

The extrapolated term is $13$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Degree is read from the first order at which differences become constant. Here the first differences themselves form an arithmetic progression with common difference $2$.

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(-3,-1,1,3,5)$$

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

Constant second differences are the fingerprint of a quadratic, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

The line through $(0,s_0)$ and $(1,s_1)$ is

$$s_n=1+(-3)n$$

$$s_4^{\text{lin}}=-11$$

$$s_4=1$$

The linear forecast misses the quadratic value at $n=4$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Only the raw row is given. Constant second differences $\Delta^{(2)}=2$ rebuild $s_n=1n^{2}-4n+1$, with axis $n=2$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — RiverFerry altitude track
tasks.context: RiverFerry overlays a linear service track on a quadratic altitude cap (figure). No formulae are printed. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The altitude curve and the linear track meet in exactly two points.
The peak of the altitude curve lies above the linear track.
The altitude curve opens downwards.
At $x=0$ the linear track sits above the altitude curve.
At the integer mark $x=1$ the altitude curve sits above the linear track.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Count the crossings on the figure, then confirm with the discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 3 x + 3$$

$$\Delta=21$$

Two crossings match a positive discriminant, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The peak is the turning point of the solid curve.

$$x=2$$

$$g\left(2\right)=6$$

$$f\left(2\right)=1$$

The peak height $6$ sits above the track height $1$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Opening is the sign of the leading coefficient of the reconstructed altitude.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 2$$

$$a=-1$$

A negative leading coefficient opens the curve downwards, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Compare the two intercepts on the vertical axis.

$$g(0)=2$$

$$f(0)=-1$$

Altitude $2$ sits above the track intercept $-1$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Read both heights at the tick $x=1$, then confirm by substituting into the reconstructed models.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 2$$

$$g(1)=5$$

$$f(x)=x - 1$$

$$f(1)=0$$

Altitude $5$ sits above the track height $0$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: The figure is the only numeric source. The models are $f(x)=x - 1$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x + 2$; vertex $\left(2,6\right)$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 2
tasks.context: A line $f$ and a parabola $g$ are compared with the mirrored pair $\tilde f(x)=f(-x)$, $\tilde g(x)=g(-x)$. No coordinates are given. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The graphs of $\tilde f$ and $\tilde g$ meet exactly as often as those of $f$ and $g$.
If $f$ and $g$ are tangent, then so are $\tilde f$ and $\tilde g$.
The difference $\tilde g-\tilde f$ stays quadratic, so the mirrored graphs meet in at most two points.
$\tilde g$ opens in the same direction as $g$.
The axis of $\tilde g$ is the reflection of the axis of $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The map $x\mapsto -x$ is a bijection of the real line, and it sends a meeting of $f$ and $g$ to a meeting of the mirrors.

$$g(x)=f(x)\iff \tilde g(-x)=\tilde f(-x)$$

The meeting count is preserved, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Tangency is a double root of $g-f$. Replacing $x$ by $-x$ sends a double root to a double root.

$$\Delta(g-f)=0\Rightarrow \Delta(\tilde g-\tilde f)=0$$

Tangency survives mirroring, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Mirroring does not raise the highest power: $\tilde g$ is still a parabola and $\tilde f$ is still a line.

$$\tilde g(x)-\tilde f(x)=a x^{2}-(b-m)x+(c-k)$$

A quadratic equation has at most two real roots, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Replacing $x$ by $-x$ leaves the leading coefficient untouched, and opening is that sign alone.

$$a_{\tilde g}=a$$

The opening direction is preserved, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The axis $x=h$ of $g$ is sent to $x=-h$ under $x\mapsto -x$, which is precisely the axis of the mirrored parabola.

$$x_{\tilde g}=-x_{g}$$

The axis is reflected, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Mirroring $x\mapsto -x$ preserves meeting count, tangency, degree and opening, and reflects the axis.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — CargoDrone leading-coefficient sweep
tasks.context: A one-parameter family $g_a(x)=ax^{2}+2x-3$ with $a\neq 0$ is tested against $f(x)=x + 1$. Study how $a$ changes meetings via $\Delta(a)$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: There is a value of $a\neq 0$ for which the line is tangent to the parabola.
For every $a>1$ the graphs miss entirely.
The axis of $g_a$ is independent of $a$.
Every parabola in the family crosses the vertical axis at $3$.
For every real $a\neq 0$ the graphs meet at least once.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Tangency is $\Delta(a)=0$. Expanding the discriminant of $g_a-f$ gives a linear equation in $a$.

$$\Delta(a)=16 a + 1$$

$$a=-\frac{1}{16}$$

A nonzero parameter produces a double root, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The discriminant $\Delta(a)=1+16a$ is positive once $a$ exceeds $-1/16$, so in particular every $a>1$ yields two meetings, not a miss.

$$\Delta(a)=16 a + 1$$

$$a>1\Rightarrow \Delta(a)>0$$

Those parameters meet twice rather than miss, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The axis formula $x=-b/(2a)$ still involves the leading coefficient.

$$x=-\frac{1}{a}$$

The axis moves when $a$ changes, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The constant term of $g_a$ does not involve $a$, but that constant is $-3$, not $3$.

$$g_a(0)=-3$$

The intercept is $-3$ for every $a$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

On the side $a<-1/16$ the discriminant is negative, so the graphs miss.

$$\Delta\left(-1\right)=-15$$

Some admissible leading coefficients produce no meeting, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Family $g_a$ versus $f(x)=x + 1$. Discriminant $\Delta(a)=16 a + 1$; tangency at $a=-1/16$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — SkiLift reconstruction
tasks.context: Engineers at SkiLift know a service line has slope $2$ and passes through $(0,-4)$. The parabola has roots $1$ and $5$ and leading coefficient $1$. Recover $f$ and $g$, then decide. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The rebuilt line is $f(x)=2 x - 4$.
The rebuilt parabola is $g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$.
Rewriting $g$ in powers of the rebuilt line gives leading coefficient $A=1$.
The rebuilt curves miss each other.
The axis of the rebuilt parabola is $x=2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Slope $2$ through the intercept $(0,-4)$ is already slope-intercept form.

$$f(x)=2 x - 4$$

The line matches the sparse data, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

A monic parabola with the two given roots expands by Vieta.

$$g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)$$

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

The expanded parabola matches the root data, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Matching $g=A f^{2}+B f+C$ starts with the square-term quotient $a/m^{2}$.

$$A=\frac{1}{2^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}$$

The rewrite coefficient is $1/4$, not $1$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The discriminant of $g-f$ decides.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 9$$

$$\Delta=28$$

A positive discriminant means two meetings, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The axis is the midpoint of the two given roots, equivalently $-b/(2a)$ after expanding $g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)=x^{2}-6x+5$.

$$x=\frac{1+5}{2}=3$$

$$x=-\frac{-6}{2\cdot 1}=3$$

The axis is $x=3$, not $x=2$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Rebuilt $f(x)=2 x - 4$, $g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$; vertex $\left(3,-4\right)$; 2 meetings; rewrite $A=\frac{1}{4}$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — BridgeDeck nested maps
tasks.context: BridgeDeck control software nests $f$ and $g$ ($f(x)=x + 2$, $g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 3$). Compare highest powers, axes, and a sample value. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The highest power of $f(g(x))$ is $x^{2}$.
The axis of $g(f)$ is $x=-1$.
The axis of $g(f)$ equals the axis of $g$.
$g(f(0))$ equals $f(g(0))$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Replace $x$ by $x+2$ in $g$ and expand.

$$g(x+2)=-(x+2)^{2}+2(x+2)+3$$

$$g(f(x))=- x^{2} - 2 x + 3$$

The expanded composition matches, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The outer map $f$ is linear, so it cannot raise the highest power of $g$. Expanding confirms a quadratic.

$$f(g(x))=- x^{2} + 2 x + 5$$

The composition $f(g(x))$ is quadratic, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Apply $-b/(2a)$ to the expanded composition $g(f)$.

$$g(f(x))=- x^{2} - 2 x + 3$$

$$x=-1$$

The axis of the composition is $x=-1$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The axis of a parabola is $-b/(2a)$ computed from that parabola's own coefficients, not inherited from an inner map. Expand $g(f)$ first.

$$g(f(x))=- x^{2} - 2 x + 3$$

$$x_{g(f)}=-1$$

The inner parabola $g$ has a different linear coefficient, so its axis is different.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 3$$

$$x_g=1$$

The axes are $-1$ and $1$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The two orders of substitution are different functions. Evaluate each at the origin by first computing the inner value.

$$f(0)=2$$

$$g(f(0))=g\left(2\right)=3$$

$$g(0)=3$$

$$f(g(0))=f\left(3\right)=5$$

The values are $3$ and $5$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Compositions $g(f(x))=- x^{2} - 2 x + 3$ and $f(g(x))=- x^{2} + 2 x + 5$. Highest powers multiply; axes of $g(f)$ and $g$ need not agree.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Observatory factored parabola
tasks.context: At Observatory the parabola is $g(x)=-(x+1)(x-3)$ and the line is $f(x)=x - 1$. Use the displayed roots together with Vieta and the discriminant. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis is $x=1$.
The product of the roots is $-3$.
The vertex height is $4$.
The line and the parabola meet twice.
The line passes through both roots of $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The axis is still the midpoint of the displayed roots; the overall minus sign does not move it.

$$x=\frac{(-1)+3}{2}=1$$

The axis is $x=1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The displayed roots multiply to $-3$. Vieta on the expanded form $g(x)=-x^{2}+2x+3$ agrees, because $P=c/a$.

$$(-1)\cdot 3=-3$$

$$P=\frac{3}{-1}=-3$$

The product is $-3$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Evaluate the factored form on the axis $x=1$, then confirm from the expanded rule $g(x)=-x^{2}+2x+3$.

$$g(1)=-(1+1)(1-3)=4$$

$$g(1)=-1+2+3=4$$

The vertex height is $4$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Expand, subtract the line, and read the discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + x + 4$$

$$\Delta=17$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

A line through both roots would be the zero function on those two abscissae, hence would have to be the zero line after two hits on a parabola's roots only if it were $y=0$. Check the given line at a root.

$$g(3)=0$$

$$f(3)=2$$

The line misses the root $x=3$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Factored $g(x)=-(x+1)(x-3)$; roots $-1,3$; axis $x=1$; $P=-3$; 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — CanalLock hybrid check
tasks.context: CanalLock supplies a figure (solid brown parabola, dashed green line) and a raw table of the solid curve's integer samples. No closed form is printed. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the figure, the solid curve opens upwards.
From the figure, the turning point of the solid curve lies below the dashed line.
From the table, successive differences show that the sampled sequence is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$.
From the table, extrapolating one step gives $s_{5}=5$.
After fitting the table, the axis is $x=2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The sketch shows a trough. The reconstructed leading coefficient confirms it.

$$g(x)=x \left(x - 4\right)$$

$$a=1$$

A positive leading coefficient opens the curve upwards, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Compare the two heights on the axis of the solid curve.

$$x=2$$

$$g\left(2\right)=-4$$

$$f\left(2\right)=-2$$

The trough height $-4$ sits below the dashed height $-2$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Differences of the raw $s_n$ row give

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

$$a=\frac{2}{2}=1$$

The table rebuilds leading coefficient $1$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The rebuilt rule $s_n=n^{2}-4n$ at the next index is

$$s_5=5^{2}-4\cdot 5=5$$

The next term is $5$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

With $a=1$ and $b=-4$ the axis formula gives

$$x=-\frac{-4}{2\cdot 1}=2$$

The fitted axis is $x=2$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Figure plus table, no printed formulae. Reconstructing gives $f(x)=2 x - 6$ and $g(x)=x \left(x - 4\right)$; axis $x=2$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — BalloonFest dense briefing
tasks.context: A briefing at BalloonFest states: a line of slope $1$ through $(4,0)$ is drawn against a monic parabola with roots $-1$ and $2$. Recover both models from that sentence. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The line and the parabola meet twice.
The axis of the parabola is $x=1$.
The product of the roots is $2$.
The slope of the line is $1$.
The vertex height is $0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The line through $(4,0)$ with slope $1$ is $f(x)=x-4$. The monic parabola with those roots is $g(x)=(x+1)(x-2)=x^{2}-x-2$. Their difference has discriminant

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 2 x + 2$$

$$\Delta=-4$$

A negative discriminant means the graphs miss, so the statement is False.

**B.** → False

The midpoint of the given roots is

$$x=\frac{-1+2}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$$

The axis is $x=\frac{1}{2}$, not $x=1$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The given roots multiply to $-2$. Vieta on the expansion $g(x)=x^{2}-x-2$ agrees.

$$P=(-1)\cdot 2=-2$$

The product is $-2$, not $2$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

The briefing states the slope directly, and point-slope through $(4,0)$ reproduces it.

$$f(x)=1\cdot (x-4)+0$$

$$f(x)=x - 4$$

The slope is $1$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Evaluate $g$ on its axis.

$$g\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{9}{4}$$

The vertex height is $-\frac{9}{4}$, not $0$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The sentence rebuilds $f(x)=x - 4$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - x - 2$. The discriminant of $g-f$ is negative, so the graphs miss; axis $x=\frac{1}{2}$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Opening, crossings, and a height comparison
tasks.context: On the axes below, a **solid brown parabola** and a **dashed green line** model clearance for WindFarm. Coefficients are not printed on the diagram. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The graphs meet in exactly two points.
The turning point of the solid curve lies above the dashed line.
The solid curve opens upwards.
At $x=0$ the dashed line sits above the solid curve.
At the integer mark $x=3$ the solid curve is higher than the dashed line.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Count the crossings on the sketch, then confirm with the discriminant of the difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 3 x + 6$$

$$\Delta=33$$

A positive discriminant matches the two visible crossings, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The axis of the reconstructed parabola is an integer tick, so both heights can be read and then checked.

$$x=1$$

$$g\left(1\right)=9$$

$$f\left(1\right)=1$$

The peak height $9$ sits above the dashed height $1$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Recover the leading coefficient from the reconstructed solid curve.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 8$$

$$a=-1$$

A negative leading coefficient opens the curve downwards, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The gap at the origin is the difference of the two intercepts.

$$g(0)=8$$

$$f(0)=2$$

The solid intercept $8$ sits above the dashed intercept $2$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Read both heights at $x=3$.

$$g(3)=5$$

$$f(3)=-1$$

The solid height $5$ sits above the dashed height $-1$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: The figure is the only source. Reconstructing the two models gives $f(x)=2 - x$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 8$. The vertex is $\left(1,9\right)$ and the graphs meet 2 times.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — SolarTrack samples
tasks.context: SolarTrack logs discrete readings $s_n$ for $n=0,1,2,\ldots$ in the table. No closed form is supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Diagnosing the table by successive differences, the leading coefficient is $-1$.
The sequence is cubic, because the later values fall.
Extrapolating one step beyond the table gives $s_{7}=-20$.
The axis of the rebuilt quadratic is $n=2$.
Stepping one index to the left of the table gives $s_{-1}=-4$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Second differences of $an^{2}+bn+c$ equal $2a$. From the raw row

$$\Delta^{(2)}=-2$$

$$a=\frac{-2}{2}=-1$$

The leading coefficient is $-1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

A cubic would have constant third differences and non-constant second differences. Here the second differences are already constant.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=-2$$

A downward-opening quadratic falls on both sides of its axis; the drop in the tail is that geometry, not a change of degree.

Constant second differences keep the degree at $2$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

With $a=-1$ and $a+b=s_1-s_0$ the remaining coefficients are $b=4$ and $c=1$.

$$s_n=-n^{2}+4n+1$$

$$s_7=-7^{2}+4\cdot 7+1=-20$$

The next term is $-20$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The axis formula uses only the first two rebuilt coefficients.

$$n=-\frac{4}{2\cdot (-1)}=2$$

The table itself mirrors about that index: $s_0=s_4$ and $s_1=s_3$.

The axis is $n=2$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The same rebuilt rule is valid at $n=-1$.

$$s_{-1}=-(-1)^{2}+4(-1)+1=-4$$

The backward extrapolation is $-4$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Only the raw row is given. Constant second differences $\Delta^{(2)}=-2$ rebuild $s_n=-1n^{2}+4n+1$, with axis $n=2$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Greenhouse climate log
tasks.context: Greenhouse logs a linear target and a quadratic temperature against hour $x$ in the table. No closed form is supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The temperature row is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$.
The target row is linear with slope $2$.
If both fitted models continue, they meet twice.
Extrapolating the temperature row one step gives the value $10$ at $x=6$.
The axis of the temperature parabola sits halfway between the two equal samples at $x=2$ and $x=3$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Second differences diagnose degree and leading coefficient.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2$$

$$a=\frac{2}{2}=1$$

Temperature is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Constant first differences of the target row are the slope.

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(2,2,2,2,2)$$

$$m=2$$

The target slope is $2$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Form the difference of the rebuilt models and read its discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 7 x + 8$$

$$\Delta=17$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The rebuilt temperature rule is $g(x)=x^{2}-5x+4$.

$$g(6)=6^{2}-5\cdot 6+4=10$$

The next temperature reading is $10$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

A parabola is symmetric about its axis, so two equal heights at integer inputs force the axis to their midpoint.

$$g(2)=g(3)=-2$$

$$x=\frac{2+3}{2}=\frac{5}{2}$$

The coefficient formula agrees.

$$x=-\frac{-5}{2\cdot 1}=\frac{5}{2}$$

The axis is $x=\frac{5}{2}$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Fitting the two rows gives $f(x)=2 x - 4$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - 5 x + 4$; axis $x=\frac{5}{2}$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 3
tasks.context: A quadratic $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$ has two distinct real roots; write $S$ for their sum and $P$ for their product. No numbers are supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: If $P<0$, the two roots have opposite signs.
If $P>0$, both roots must be positive.
If $S=0$, the product $P$ must be positive.
If $P>0$ and $S<0$, both roots are positive.
If $P<0$ and $a>0$, then $g(0)>0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The product of the roots is $P$. A negative product means one factor is positive and the other is negative.

$$r_{1}r_{2}=P<0$$

Opposite signs follow from a negative product, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

A positive product only forces the two roots to share a sign. Combined with a negative sum they are both negative.

$$P>0,\quad S<0\Rightarrow r_{1},r_{2}<0$$

A positive product does not force both roots to be positive, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

A vanishing sum means the roots are opposites $r$ and $-r$, so their product is $-r^{2}$. For two distinct real roots that quantity is strictly negative.

$$S=0\Rightarrow P=-r^{2}<0$$

The product is negative, not positive, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Equal signs come from the product; the shared sign is read from the sum. A negative sum puts both roots to the left of the origin.

$$P>0,\ S<0\Rightarrow r_{1}<0,\ r_{2}<0$$

Both roots are negative, not positive, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The constant term is $g(0)=c=aP$. A positive leading coefficient times a negative product makes $c$ negative.

$$g(0)=aP<0$$

The origin lies below the graph, so $g(0)$ is negative, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Vieta: $S=-b/a$ and $P=c/a$. Sign patterns of the roots follow from $S$ and $P$ alone; $g(0)=aP$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — FilmSet sliding line
tasks.context: Lines $f_k(x)=2x+k$ slide vertically against $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+3$ at FilmSet. Decide which inequalities on $k$ force two meetings, tangency, or a miss. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Exactly one value of $k$ gives tangency, namely $k=-6$.
Whenever $k>-6$, the line meets the parabola twice.
Whenever $k<-7$, the line meets the parabola twice.
When $k=0$ the line misses the parabola.
For every real $k$ the line meets the parabola.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The discriminant of $g-f_k$ is linear in $k$, so it has exactly one root.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 24$$

$$k=-6$$

Tangency occurs at the unique root $k=-6$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The leading coefficient of $\Delta(k)$ is positive, so $\Delta$ is positive to the right of its root.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 24$$

$$k>-6\Rightarrow \Delta(k)>0$$

That half-line is exactly the two-meeting zone, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

For $k<-6$ the discriminant is negative. The stricter inequality $k<-7$ sits inside that miss region.

$$\Delta(-8)=-8$$

Those shifts miss the parabola, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Substitute $k=0$ into the discriminant.

$$\Delta(0)=24$$

A positive discriminant at $k=0$ gives two meetings, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Pushing $k$ past $-6$ into the negative-$\Delta$ region makes the graphs miss.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 24$$

Some vertical shifts miss the parabola, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Sliding lines $f_k=2x+k$ versus $g=x^{2}-4x+3$. Discriminant $\Delta(k)=4 k + 24$; tangency at $k=-6$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — MineCart reconstruction
tasks.context: Rebuild for MineCart: line slope $-1$, point $(2,3)$; parabola axis $x=1$, vertex height $4$, leading coefficient $-1$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The rebuilt line is $f(x)=5 - x$.
The rebuilt parabola is $g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 3$.
The rebuilt curves meet in exactly two points.
The vertex height is $2$.
The rewrite $g=A f^{2}+B f+C$ has $A=1$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Point-slope with slope $-1$ through $(2,3)$ expands to

$$f(x)=-1\cdot (x-2)+3$$

$$f(x)=5 - x$$

The line matches the given slope and point, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Vertex form with axis $x=1$, height $4$, and leading coefficient $-1$ expands to

$$g(x)=-\left(x-1\right)^{2}+4$$

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 3$$

The expanded parabola matches the vertex data, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Form the difference and read the discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 3 x - 2$$

$$\Delta=1$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The vertex height was part of the given data and can be rechecked by substitution.

$$g\left(1\right)=4$$

The vertex height is $4$, not $2$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The leading rewrite coefficient is the quotient of the two leading coefficients, with the line's slope squared in the denominator.

$$A=\frac{-1}{-1^{2}}=-1$$

The coefficient $A$ is $-1$, not $1$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Rebuilt $f(x)=5 - x$, $g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 3$; vertex $\left(1,4\right)$; 2 meetings; rewrite $A=-1$.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — FloodGate nested maps
tasks.context: A line $f(x)=3 x + 1$ and parabola $g(x)=x \left(x - 2\right)$ are nested in both orders at FloodGate. Track highest powers, axes, and meetings with the horizontal axis. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis of $g(f)$ is the vertical axis.
The graph of $g(f)$ meets the horizontal axis in two real points.
The highest power of $g(g(x))$ is $x^{2}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Substitute the line into $g(x)=x^{2}-2x$ and expand.

$$(3x+1)^{2}-2(3x+1)$$

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 1$$

The composition simplifies to $9x^{2}-1$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The other order applies the line to $g$ itself.

$$f(g(x))=3(x^{2}-2x)+1$$

$$f(g(x))=3 x^{2} - 6 x + 1$$

The expanded $f(g(x))$ matches, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

After expansion $g(f)$ has no linear term, so $-b/(2a)$ is zero.

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 1$$

$$x=0$$

The axis of $g(f)$ is $x=0$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Set the expanded composition equal to zero.

$$9x^{2}-1=0$$

$$x=\pm\frac{1}{3}$$

Two distinct real zeros sit on the horizontal axis, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Nesting a quadratic in itself multiplies the degrees: $2\cdot 2=4$. Expanding makes the fourth power visible.

$$g(g(x))=x \left(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 2 x + 4\right)$$

The highest power is $x^{4}$, not $x^{2}$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Compositions $g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 1$ and $f(g(x))=3 x^{2} - 6 x + 1$. Highest powers multiply; axes of $g(f)$ and $g$ need not agree.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Harvester factored parabola
tasks.context: At Harvester the parabola is $g(x)=(x-1)(x-4)$ and the line is $f(x)=2 x - 3$. Combine Vieta with the discriminant of $g-f$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis is the midpoint $x=\frac{5}{2}$.
The product of the roots is $4$.
The sum of the roots is $5$.
The discriminant of $g-f$ is positive, so the graphs meet twice.
The value $g(0)$ equals the product of the roots.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The midpoint of the displayed roots is the axis.

$$x=\frac{1+4}{2}=\frac{5}{2}$$

The axis is $x=\frac{5}{2}$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Vieta: for a monic quadratic the product equals the constant term.

$$P=1\cdot 4=4$$

The product is $4$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Vieta: the sum is $-b/a$, which for a monic quadratic is the unsigned linear coefficient.

$$S=1+4=5$$

$$S=-\frac{-5}{1}=5$$

The sum is $5$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Expand $g$, subtract the line, and compute the discriminant.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 7 x + 7$$

$$\Delta=21$$

A positive discriminant gives two meetings, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

For a monic quadratic, $g(0)=c$ and Vieta says $P=c$. Directly from the factors

$$g(0)=(-1)(-4)=4$$

$$P=4$$

Both quantities equal $4$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Factored $g(x)=(x-1)(x-4)$; roots $1,4$; axis $x=\frac{5}{2}$; $P=4$; 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — DockCrane hybrid check
tasks.context: DockCrane supplies a figure (solid brown parabola, dashed green line) and a raw table of the solid curve's integer samples. No closed form is printed. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the figure, the solid curve opens upwards.
From the figure, the graphs meet in exactly three points.
From the table, the first differences are constant, so $s_n$ is linear.
From the table, extrapolating one step gives $s_{4}=-4$.
After fitting the table, the axis is $x=0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The sketch shows a peak. The reconstructed leading coefficient is negative.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 4$$

$$a=-1$$

The solid curve opens downwards, so the statement is False.

**B.** → False

A line and a parabola cannot meet three times. The discriminant of the difference confirms the actual count.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + x + 3$$

$$\Delta=13$$

Two meetings occur, not three, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The first differences of the raw row are not constant.

$$\Delta^{(1)}=(1,-1,-3)$$

$$\Delta^{(2)}=-2$$

Constant second differences keep the sequence quadratic, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Rebuild $s_n=-n^{2}+2n+4$ from $\Delta^{{(2)}}=-2$ together with the opening step and $s_0$, then substitute $n=4$.

$$s_4=-4^{2}+2\cdot 4+4=-4$$

The next term is $-4$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Second differences of the raw row recover $2a=-2$, so $a=-1$. The opening first difference is $a+b=s_1-s_0=1$, hence $b=2$.

$$a=-1,\quad b=2$$

$$x=-\frac{2}{2\cdot (-1)}=1$$

An axis at $x=0$ would have required a vanishing linear coefficient.

The axis is $x=1$, not $x=0$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Figure plus table, no printed formulae. Reconstructing gives $f(x)=x + 1$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 2 x + 4$; axis $x=1$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — PortPilot dense briefing
tasks.context: PortPilot's note reads: a line of slope $2$ through $(0,1)$ is set against a parabola that opens downwards, has roots $1$ and $5$, and leading coefficient $-1$. Recover both models. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis of the parabola is $x=3$.
The parabola opens downwards.
The line and the parabola meet twice.
The vertex height is $0$.
The product of the roots is $-5$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The axis is the midpoint of the given roots, independent of the leading-coefficient sign.

$$x=\frac{1+5}{2}=3$$

The axis is $x=3$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The briefing names leading coefficient $-1$, which is the opening test.

$$g(x)=-(x-1)(x-5)$$

$$a=-1$$

A negative leading coefficient opens the parabola downwards, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The line through $(0,1)$ with slope $2$ is $f(x)=2x+1$. Subtract from the expanded $g$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} + 4 x - 6$$

$$\Delta=-8$$

A negative discriminant means the graphs miss, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The axis is the midpoint $x=3$ of the given roots. Evaluate the factored form $g(x)=-(x-1)(x-5)$ there.

$$g(3)=-(3-1)(3-5)=4$$

The expansion $-x^{2}+6x-5$ returns the same height.

$$g(3)=-9+18-5=4$$

The vertex height is $4$, not $0$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The displayed roots multiply to $5$. Vieta on $g(x)=-x^{2}+6x-5$ gives $P=c/a=(-5)/(-1)=5$ as well.

$$P=1\cdot 5=5$$

The product is $5$, not $-5$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The note rebuilds $f(x)=2 x + 1$ and $g(x)=- x^{2} + 6 x - 5$; axis $x=3$, vertex height $4$, 0 meetings.
